title: This Mammal's Body Gets Colder Than Ice and It Wakes Up Fine

scenes.text: One mammal's body gets colder than ice, and it wakes up alive.
It's the arctic ground squirrel. In Alaska it hibernates for seven or eight months.
Scientists at the University of Alaska measured it at minus two point nine degrees Celsius, the lowest ever recorded in a mammal.
Its body supercools below freezing without turning to ice.
Every two or three weeks it shivers for hours to warm back up near ninety-eight degrees, then drops again.
Then spring arrives, and it walks out like nothing happened.

description:
The arctic ground squirrel's body can drop to minus 2.9 degrees Celsius in hibernation, the coldest ever measured in a mammal.
It supercools below freezing without turning to ice.
Could you sleep through a winter?
first_comment: Would you hibernate for seven months if you could?
